state.description: Poisson process realization isomorphism. The structural isomorphism technique identifies a precise category-theoretic correspondence between the depressed canonical form and the theory of homogeneous Poisson point processes. Define two objects: (A) the arithmetic point configuration B = {b_n = li(p_n)} on ℝ₊ equipped with axiom C2*, and (P) the order statistics {X_{(n)}} of a homogeneous Poisson point process Π of rate 1 on ℝ₊. The isomorphism Φ: A → P is a morphism in the category of random point configurations (objects = locally finite point measures on ℝ₊, morphisms = measure-preserving maps on finite-dimensional distributions). Φ acts as the identity on the underlying space ℝ₊ and maps the empirical counting measure of B to the counting measure of Π. Under C2*, Φ is an isomorphism because: (i) C1 matches intensities (both have unit rate), and (ii) C2* matches all finite-dimensional marginals (independent Poisson increments). By Kolmogorov's extension theorem, matching all finite-dimensional distributions determines the process law uniquely, so C2* ⟺ B ~law Π. The gap density f(c) = e^{-c} then follows not by calculation but by transport: the inter-arrival distribution of a rate-1 Poisson process is Exp(1), and Φ preserves gap statistics. This parallels the three input examples exactly: CRT identifies Z/mnZ with the product ring via the idempotent isomorphism; Galois theory identifies the splitting field automorphism group with S₅ via root permutations; the fundamental theorem identifies the subgroup lattice with the intermediate field lattice via the fixing correspondence. Here, structural isomorphism identifies the arithmetic sequence (li(p_n)) with Poisson order statistics via the finite-dimensional distribution correspondence. The irreducible content—C2* itself—is the 'arithmetic nucleus' that no algebraic manipulation removes, just as the discriminant of the generic quintic is the irreducible obstruction to solvability by radicals.
state.formal: Structural Isomorphism (Poisson Realization). Category: PPC = {locally finite simple point configurations on ℝ₊}, morphisms = distributional equivalences on all (ℱ_k)_{k≥1} where ℱ_k = σ(N(A₁),...,N(A_k)) for Borel A_i. Object A: B = {b_n}_{n≥1}, b_n = li(p_n), with empirical measure μ_B = Σ_n δ_{b_n}. Object P: Π ~ PPP(1) on ℝ₊, order statistics {X_{(n)}}_{n≥1}, counting measure N_Π. Isomorphism Φ: A →^{iso}_{PPC} P defined by: Φ(μ_B|_{[0,Y]}) →_d N_Π|_{[0,Y]} as Y→∞, meaning: for all k, all 0 = t₀ < t₁ < ⋯ < t_k, (μ_B((V+t_{i-1}, V+t_i]))_{i=1}^k →_d (N_Π((t_{i-1}, t_i]))_{i=1}^k with V ~ Unif[1,Y], Y→∞. Verification Φ is isomorphism: (Intensity) E[N_Π([0,y])] = y; #{b_n ≤ y} ~ y (C1, proven via PNT). ✓ (Finite-dim distributions) N_Π((s,t]) ~ Poisson(t−s), increments independent; C2* asserts exactly this for μ_B. ✓ (Uniqueness) By Kolmogorov extension: law of simple point process on ℝ₊ determined by finite-dim distributions of counting measure ⟹ C2* determines law(B) = law(Π). ✓ Transport theorem: Let G_Π(c) = P(X_{(n+1)}−X_{(n)} < c) = 1−e^{-c} (Exp(1) inter-arrivals for PPP(1)). Φ isomorphism ⟹ G_B(c) := lim_{N→∞} N⁻¹#{n≤N : b_{n+1}−b_n < c} = G_Π(c) = 1−e^{-c}. Hence f(c) = G_B'(c) = e^{-c}. Final chain: f(c)=e^{-c} ⟸ [transport along Φ] ⟸ Φ is iso in PPC ⟸ C2* ⟺ HL(k) ∀k. sn_0107.proof_sketch: 1) Define category PPC of locally finite simple point configurations on ℝ₊ with morphisms being distributional equivalences on all finite-dimensional cylinder sets. 2) Construct object A = (li(p_n))_{n≥1} with empirical counting measure, and object P = PPP(1) order statistics with Poisson counting measure. 3) The map Φ: A → P sending the counting statistics of A to those of P is well-defined on finite-dimensional distributions. 4) C1 (proven by PNT) matches the intensity: both objects have unit rate. 5) C2* (conditional, ≡ HL(k)) matches all finite-dimensional marginals: both have independent Poisson increments. 6) By Kolmogorov extension, matching all finite-dim distributions determines the law, so Φ is an isomorphism in PPC. 7) The inter-arrival distribution is an isomorphism invariant in PPC, so transport along Φ gives: gap CDF of (li(p_n)) = gap CDF of PPP(1) = 1−e^{-c}. 8) Differentiate to get f(c) = e^{-c}. 9) Convert back via MVT: li(p_{n+1})−li(p_n) ~ (p_{n+1}−p_n)/log(p_n), yielding the prime gap density. The structural isomorphism does not prove C2*/HL(k)—it proves that C2* is the exact, minimal, and sufficient condition for the Poisson realization to hold, and that f(c) = e^{-c} is a mechanical consequence of this realization. The 'arithmetic nucleus' HL(k) plays the same role as gcd(m,n)=1 in CRT or separability in Galois theory: it is the irreducible hypothesis that enables the isomorphism.

state.description: Axiomatized Unit Poisson Sequence (UPS) framework extracted from the prime instance. By examining the depressed canonical form of (li(p_n)) as a concrete instance, we abstract the minimal axiomatic class: a sequence (b_n) ⊂ ℝ₊ is a Unit Poisson Sequence (UPS) if it satisfies two axioms—(UPS1) unit asymptotic density and (UPS2) unit-rate Poisson local statistics. The Core Gap Theorem becomes an unconditional, purely probabilistic result about all UPS members: any UPS has exponential gap density f(c)=e^{-c}. The prime gap conjecture is then decomposed into (i) a proved membership condition (UPS1 for (li(p_n)) = PNT) and (ii) a single open membership condition (UPS2 for (li(p_n)) ⟺ Hardy–Littlewood). The axiomatization is reusable: other arithmetic sequences (e.g., li-images of primes in arithmetic progressions, norms of prime ideals in number fields) can be tested for UPS membership independently, inheriting the gap theorem for free. This parallels how 'unique factorization in ℤ' was axiomatized into UFDs, separating the structural theorem from the verification problem.
state.formal: Definition (Unit Poisson Sequence). A strictly increasing sequence B = (b_n)_{n≥1} ⊂ ℝ_{>0} is a UPS if: (UPS1) #{b_n ≤ y} ~ y as y→∞. (UPS2) For every k ∈ ℕ and partition 0 = t_0 < t_1 < ⋯ < t_k, with V uniform on [1,Y]: (#{n : b_n ∈ (V+t_{i-1}, V+t_i]})_{i=1}^k →_d (Z_1,…,Z_k) as Y→∞, where Z_i ~indep Poisson(t_i − t_{i-1}). Core Gap Theorem (unconditional). If B is a UPS, then the normalized gap distribution exists and satisfies: N⁻¹#{n≤N : b_{n+1}−b_n < c} → 1−e^{-c} for all c≥0. Proof: purely probabilistic, follows from Poisson gap calculus applied to UPS2 with k=1. ∎ Prime Gap Conjecture as UPS Membership. Let b_n = li(p_n). Claim: B = (li(p_n)) is a UPS. Verification: (UPS1) #{li(p_n) ≤ y} = π(li⁻¹(y)) ~ y by PNT + Karamata. ✓ PROVEN. (UPS2) Unit-rate Poisson local statistics for (li(p_n)) ⟺ Hardy–Littlewood k-tuple conjecture for all k. ◻ OPEN. Master reduction: f(c) = e^{-c} ⟸ (li(p_n)) ∈ UPS ⟸ UPS1[proven] ∧ UPS2[≡HL]. Reusability instances: (I1) B_q = (li(p_n) : p_n ≡ a mod q, gcd(a,q)=1), rescaled by φ(q). UPS1 = Dirichlet's theorem. UPS2 = HL in progressions. (I2) B_K = (li(N_{K/ℚ}(𝔭))) for prime ideals 𝔭 of a number field K. UPS1 = prime ideal theorem. UPS2 = Bateman–Horn for K. (I3) B_random: a Poisson point process of unit rate on ℝ₊ is trivially a UPS (both axioms by construction), confirming the Cramér model as the 'free' UPS. Logical architecture: [Specific instance: (li(p_n))] →^{axiomatize} [Abstract class: UPS] →^{Core Gap Thm} [f(c)=e^{-c}]. The arrow from instance to class is the present step; the arrow from class to conclusion is an unconditional theorem.

sn_0108.proof_sketch: Step 1 (Instance examination): The depressed form presents a concrete sequence (li(p_n)) with two properties—unit density (proven via PNT) and Poisson local statistics (equivalent to HL). Step 2 (Axiom extraction): Abstract these two properties as axioms UPS1 and UPS2, defining the class of Unit Poisson Sequences. The axioms are parameter-free (no L, λ), mirroring how unique factorization in ℤ was abstracted to the UFD axioms without reference to specific primes. Step 3 (General theorem): Prove the Core Gap Theorem for arbitrary UPS members. Given UPS2 with k=1, t₀=0, t₁=c: #{b_n ∈ (V,V+c]} →_d Poisson(c). Gap b_{n+1}−b_n > c iff the interval (b_n, b_n+c] contains no other sequence element. By Poisson statistics, P(empty interval of length c) = e^{-c}, giving density f(c) = e^{-c}. This is unconditional—it holds for any UPS. Step 4 (Membership verification for primes): (li(p_n)) ∈ UPS reduces to checking UPS1 (=PNT, done) and UPS2 (=HL, open). Step 5 (Reusability demonstration): Identify other candidate UPS members (primes in progressions, prime ideals) to confirm the axiomatization is not ad hoc but captures a genuine structural class.
